rule: First trial is lead-finding-only until Candidate Profile, Application Rules, and Resume Routing have verified facts.
reason: Prevents accidental real submissions before high-impact facts are known.

rule: Stop for CAPTCHA, Cloudflare, login, 2FA, account switching, payment, permission prompts, or unclear legal, identity, work authorization, sponsorship, or compensation questions.
reason: ApplyPilot safety boundary.

rule: For voluntary self-ID, leave blank, choose Prefer not to say, decline, or skip when available unless exact user-approved answers exist.
reason: No identity information may be guessed.

rule: Do not upload or route a resume until the user confirms the exact file path and role family.
reason: No verified resume file has been selected.

rule: Use the Simplify/Coder Quad new-grad list as a high-signal early-career source because it includes role age, new-grad category, locations, ATS links, and sponsorship/citizenship icons.
reason: It produced fresh 0d leads matching the user's target role families.

rule: Skip postings marked or described as space, aerospace, defense, military, security-clearance, US-citizenship, or US-person restricted before deeper fit review.
reason: This catches hard constraints early and prevents wasting review time.

rule: When querying job URLs from zsh, quote URLs that contain '?' or '&' so shell globbing does not break API/feed fetches.
reason: Unquoted ATS URLs can fail locally before any network request is made.

rule: For command-line lead finding, LinkedIn, Simplify, YC, Built In, Google search, and Handshake were reachable; Wellfound and Indeed returned HTTP 403 and should be retried through browser/manual review if needed.
reason: Avoid treating source access errors as candidate/job fit signals.

rule: For new-grad and early-career lead finding, prioritize Simplify/Coder Quad feed, LinkedIn guest search, and Built In entry-level pages because they returned parseable public job data from the command line.
reason: These sources produced actionable rows with title, company, location, age or posted date, and application/detail URLs.

rule: Treat Indeed and Wellfound command-line results as source-limited when they return captcha, anti-bot, JavaScript, or ad-blocker interstitial pages.
reason: Do not bypass anti-bot controls; retry manually/browser-side only if the user wants those sources checked.
source_blocker_or_lesson: Indeed captcha-like page; Wellfound JS/ad-blocker interstitial

rule: Use YC Work at a Startup only when listings explicitly match sponsorship, salary, level, and role filters; many YC role-page rows are senior, old, below salary floor, or visa-limited.
reason: YC pages were parseable but did not produce many safe early-career sponsorship-compatible leads in this batch.
source_blocker_or_lesson: YC role pages parseable but low yield for current constraints

rule: Skip Amazon subsidiaries or postings whose public detail clearly routes compensation/employment framing through Amazon when the user has Amazon as a company hard skip.
reason: Twitch looked like a good SWE1 lead but the detail page referenced Amazon compensation, so it should not enter the pending queue without user override.

rule: Skip any posting when the job title explicitly says 'C++'.
reason: User requested excluding explicitly C++-titled roles from the pending/application queue.

rule: Keep the search new-grad focused: skip Product Manager/Product Management roles and skip SDE II, Software Engineer II, level 2, mid-level, senior, staff, principal, lead, manager, architect, and other non-new-grad seniority signals.
reason: User clarified they are a new grad and does not want Product Manager or higher-level engineering roles in the queue.

rule: For daily searches, treat postings with age markers like 1mo, 2mo, month, year, almost, or over as stale unless the user explicitly asks to include older exceptional roles.
reason: The Simplify feed contains many old roles that otherwise match title/location but should not crowd the new-grad review queue.

rule: Skip LinkedIn rows when the visible company name conflicts with the job body or recruiting/legal text, and prefer direct company/ATS source-of-truth pages.
reason: Two LinkedIn new-grad AI rows showed unrelated company names while the detail body referenced Notion recruiting text.

rule: Skip postings that ask U.S. citizenship or security-clearance questions even when the title and level otherwise match.
reason: Wyetech Software Engineer 1 asked U.S. citizenship and clearance-status questions on the public Lever page.

rule: Indeed and Wellfound remain source-limited from command-line access when they return captcha, JavaScript, or ad-blocker interstitial pages; do not bypass those controls.
reason: Today Indeed returned captcha/blocking content and Wellfound returned JS/ad-blocker interstitial content.

rule: For new-grad eligibility, keep postings that accept graduation dates between December 2026 and May 2027; skip postings that explicitly require a graduation date outside that window.
reason: User added a graduation-window screening rule for lead finding and application review.

rule: Include AI Engineer and similar new-grad technical AI titles in future searches, including ML Engineer, Machine Learning Engineer, Applied AI Engineer, AI/ML Software Engineer, LLM Engineer, and Agentic AI Engineer.
reason: User explicitly requested AI Engineer or similar titles be included in future searches.

rule: LinkedIn Premium personal search is an allowed lead source only through an already-authenticated user session or user-provided/exported leads; never request credentials or bypass login, 2FA, CAPTCHA, or account prompts.
reason: User has LinkedIn Premium and asked to use personal search.

rule: Do not include postings whose company is listed only as Stealth Startup in future searches.
reason: User requested excluding Stealth Startup leads going forward.

rule: Search public Ashby hosted job boards and Ashby posting pages during future lead finding when they appear in feeds, company career pages, or targeted searches.
reason: Ashby public postings were useful source-of-truth pages for Notion and Cerebras leads and expose role text, location, salary, and graduation/level requirements without needing an account.

rule: Skip any posting when the job title includes 'PhD' or the posting explicitly targets/requires PhD candidates.
reason: User requested excluding PhD roles now and in future lead searches.

rule: Skip new-grad postings when the direct source-of-truth page requires a full-time start date before the candidate's stored graduation window.
reason: A Notion direct Ashby new-grad posting required starting full-time prior to July 27 2026, which conflicts with the candidate's December 2026 through May 2027 graduation window.

rule: Do not include postings from CGI in future searches.
reason: User requested excluding CGI from the job search workflow.

rule: Do not include postings from BeaconFire in future searches.
reason: User requested excluding BeaconFire from the job search workflow.

rule: Do not include postings from Hired in future searches.
reason: User requested excluding Hired from the job search workflow.

rule: Do not include postings from Cerebras Systems or Cerebras in future searches.
reason: User requested excluding Cerebras Systems because its roles require US clearance.

rule: For ByteDance/TikTok graduate roles, choose the top two positions before applying because source pages say candidates can apply to a maximum of two positions across ByteDance and affiliates globally.
reason: Prevents wasting the limited application slots on lower-fit duplicate graduate roles from the same affiliated employer.

rule: Exclude TikTok and ByteDance from lead finding and application review until 2027-01-01.
reason: User requested excluding TikTok and ByteDance until 2027-01-01.

rule: For a Dec 2026-May 2027 graduation window, search the 2027 new-grad cohort trackers, not the 2026 cohort.
reason: By Aug 2026 most 2026-cohort new-grad Ashby/Greenhouse reqs (e.g. Benchling, Replit, Harvey) are closed and target earlier graduation dates outside the candidate window.

rule: Exclude T-Mobile from lead finding and application review.
reason: User requested excluding T-Mobile on 2026-08-13.

rule: Skip Crowe postings for lead finding while their reqs state 'Crowe is not sponsoring for work authorization at this time.'
reason: Two Crowe reqs on 2026-08-16 (Machine Learning Software Engineer 1 and AI Technical Consultant) carried an explicit no-sponsorship statement, which conflicts with the F-1 OPT/STEM OPT and future-sponsorship requirement.

rule: Skip Fidelity Investments Leap Software Engineer cohorts; the postings state Fidelity will not provide immigration sponsorship.
reason: All three 2027 Leap cohorts (January, April, July) found on 2026-08-16 carry the same no-sponsorship line, so future Leap reqs can be skipped without re-reading each one.

rule: Verify the employer's real country before trusting the tracker location column; 'Ontario, CA' can mean Ontario, Canada.
reason: Two Sun Life 'Ontario, CA' rows on 2026-08-16 resolved to North York, Ontario, Canada in the Workday URL, which is outside the US work-authorization policy.

rule: Read the posting body for salary floor and advanced-degree targeting before marking a Workday/Ashby lead Pending.
reason: On 2026-08-16 the posting bodies alone disqualified Micron (Master's/PhD targeting, 113k floor), Crowe (62k-100k), and MiTek (90k-110k) that all looked like clean new-grad matches from the tracker row.

rule: When the speedyapply trackers return almost no fresh 0-1d rows, sweep the Greenhouse and Ashby company board APIs directly before closing out the fetch.
reason: On 2026-08-17 both trackers plus the Simplify board yielded only 4 unique new postings, all skips; a direct company-board sweep surfaced the one real match of the day (Roblox 2027 Early Career).

rule: Treat the standard Roblox sponsorship paragraph as one recurring open question rather than re-triaging it per req.
reason: The same hedged 'may not support future H-1B sponsorship' wording appeared on every Roblox req seen on 2026-08-16 and 2026-08-17; a single user decision unblocks all of them at once.

rule: Do not re-run a full fetch the same day; the speedyapply trackers refresh roughly daily and a same-day repeat mostly re-reads unchanged data.
reason: A second 2026-08-17 fetch found both speedyapply files byte-identical to the earlier pull, and a widened 247-board Greenhouse/Ashby/Lever sweep returned zero reqs posted since 2026-08-16. Only the Simplify board had moved, adding 4 rows that were all skips.

rule: Exclude Roblox from lead finding and application review.
reason: User requested excluding Roblox on 2026-08-17.

rule: Exclude CVS Health from lead finding and application review.
reason: User requested excluding CVS on 2026-08-17.

rule: When the speedyapply 2027 SWE and AI new-grad trackers return fewer than about five fresh 0-1d rows, broaden to the Simplify/Coder Quad new-grad board in the same pass instead of ending the fetch.
reason: On 2026-08-18 the two speedyapply trackers together produced only three 0-1d rows, one of them an excluded company, while the Simplify board produced 15. The same pattern appeared on 2026-08-17.

rule: Classify a posting whose listed pay range straddles the 120,000 USD floor as Pending and flag it for a user decision, rather than skipping it. Skip only when the entire listed range sits below the floor.
reason: The salary rule skips postings whose listed base salary is below 120,000 USD, which is unambiguous for Medtronic at 74,400-111,600 but not for Charta Health at 90,000-140,000 or Disney at 97,500-136,900. Treating a straddling range as an automatic skip would have discarded two of the four real matches on 2026-08-18.

rule: Read shortlisted postings through public ATS JSON endpoints rather than page scrapes: Apple jobs.apple.com/api/v1/jobDetails/<id>, Ashby non-user-graphql ApiJobPosting with descriptionHtml, BambooHR /careers/<id>/detail, Workday /wday/cxs/<tenant>/<site>/job/<path>, and SmartRecruiters api.smartrecruiters.com/v1/companies/<co>/postings/<id>.
reason: All five endpoints returned full posting text on 2026-08-18, which is what let citizenship, clearance, level, and salary language be verified for every shortlisted lead in one pass. Note that Ashby rejects descriptionPlain and requires descriptionHtml.

rule: Exclude The Walt Disney Company, including Disney Entertainment, ESPN, Hulu, and ABC, from lead finding and application review.
reason: User requested excluding The Walt Disney Company on 2026-08-18.

rule: Parse the speedyapply NEW_GRAD_USA.md files, not README.md; the repo root README lists internships.
reason: The 2027 SWE and AI repos both put new-grad rows in NEW_GRAD_USA.md while README.md holds the internship table, so a fetch that reads only README.md screens the wrong cohort.

rule: Distrust the tracker salary column; read the posting body before treating a headline number as the offer.
reason: On 2026-08-19 the tracker showed Five Rings LINK 2027 at 381k/yr, but the body describes a five-day sophomore workshop paying a 2,000 USD stipend. The same pass found Charles Schwab listing pay hourly at 43.27-44.23 USD, which no tracker column surfaces as roughly 90,000 USD annualized.

rule: Check what the company actually builds before trusting a generic software title; the space and defense skip is often invisible in the title and location.
reason: Apex Technology's Los Angeles 'Software Engineer, Engineering Systems' req reads as an ordinary full-stack role until the body identifies the company as a satellite bus manufacturer and requires all applicants to be a U.S. Person. STR's 'Associate Software Engineer' in San Diego is likewise national security R&D requiring a clearance.

rule: When a Simplify board row shows the closed-application lock and no posting URL, record it as Skipped for a closed application rather than hunting for a live link.
reason: The OKX AI-Native Mobile Engineer New Grad row on 2026-08-19 was a Tier 1 San Jose new-grad match by title but carried the closed marker in place of an apply link, so there was nothing to screen.

rule: The Simplify/Coder Quad README is an HTML <table>, not a markdown pipe table; parse <tr>/<td> blocks or the fetch silently returns zero rows.
reason: A pipe-table parser matched nothing against the current README even though the board held 21 fresh 0-1d rows, which would have read as an empty board rather than a parser failure.

rule: Run ATS and board API calls through curl, not Python urllib; urllib fails with CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED in this environment while curl to the same URL returns 200.
reason: A 154-board sweep returned 154 errors and looked like a total source outage until the failure was traced to missing local CA certificates in Python.

rule: Do not treat the Greenhouse board list API's updated_at as a posting date; filter candidates by title and location first, then confirm freshness with first_published on the job detail endpoint.
reason: The 154-board sweep returned 4,053 reqs 'since 2026-08-18' because updated_at churns on old requisitions; title and location filtering cut that to three rows, all skips.

rule: Read the first line of a Workday body before shortlisting a new-grad AI req; the sponsorship exclusion is often stated above the job description rather than in the qualifications.
reason: General Motors' New College Graduate AI & Data Engineering req opened with 'GM does not provide immigration-related sponsorship for this role', which no tracker column surfaces and which killed the strongest AI row of 2026-08-20.

rule: When a posting is badged new grad or new college graduate but the body asks the hire to set architecture strategy or act as a technical authority, hold it for a user decision rather than treating the badge as the level.
reason: GlobalFoundries' AI/ML Software Engineer (2026 New College Graduate) req requires expertise in CPU and SoC architecture and MLIR/IREE compiler infrastructure and asks the hire to lead workload-driven architecture strategy, which is not new-grad scope.

rule: On a dry day, the direct company-board sweep is the only source that produces leads, but nearly all of its hits are already tracked; dedupe against job_pool before reading any body.
reason: On 2026-08-21 the sweep returned 89 title-and-location matches across 71 reachable boards and only 3 were new, all of which became the day's pending leads. Both trackers and the Simplify board produced nothing.

rule: Treat a campus or cohort requisition as fresh for its whole recruiting cycle rather than skipping it on first_published; check the interview start date instead.
reason: Five Rings' Campus Full Time 2027 - Software Developer was first published 2026-07-14, five weeks outside the freshness window, but states that interviews begin September 2026, so it is an open 2027 cohort req and not a stale posting.

rule: When a company posts the same role under two start dates, track both rather than folding one into the other, and read both bodies; sibling reqs can differ on compensation disclosure.
reason: Freeform's New Grad December 2026 req lists 125,000-150,000 USD while its otherwise identical New Grad Summer 2027 sibling, screened on 2026-08-20, lists no salary at all. Reading only one would have left an open compensation question that the other req answers.

rule: A C++-heavy body under a title that does not say C++ is a user decision, not an automatic skip; the title-based rule does not fire but the user should rule on it.
reason: Five Rings' Campus Full Time 2027 - Software Developer is a 300,000 USD Tier 1 New York campus match whose work is explicitly C++ on Linux. The same question came up on the Five Rings LINK req on 2026-08-19 and will recur across quant firms.

rule: Exclude Bot Auto from lead finding and application review.
reason: User requested excluding Bot Auto on 2026-08-21.

rule: Dedupe on a normalized company name, not a raw substring; strip spaces and case from both the pool value and the query before comparing, and check the job title too.
reason: On 2026-08-21 the Bot Auto dedupe searched for the ATS-token spelling botauto, which matched only the one pool row whose URL contained it and missed two rows stored under the display name Bot Auto. One of those was the same requisition as the lead being added, so a duplicate entered the pool.
